back_blocks.md: A **reversible reaction** is one in which the products can react to re-form the original **reactants**, so the reaction can proceed in both the forward and the reverse direction.

cards.back_md: A **reversible reaction** is one in which the products can react to re-form the original **reactants**, so the reaction can proceed in both the forward and the reverse direction.

front_blocks.md: What symbol is used in equations to show a reversible reaction?

back_blocks.md: The symbol **⇌** is used, with two half-arrowheads pointing in opposite directions to show the **forward** and **reverse** reactions occurring simultaneously.

front_blocks.md: Heating ammonium chloride causes it to decompose into **..........** gas and **..........** chloride gas, and these gases recombine on cooling to reform the solid.

back_blocks.md: Heating ammonium chloride causes it to decompose into **ammonia** gas and **hydrogen** chloride gas, and these gases recombine on cooling to reform the solid.

cards.front_md: Heating ammonium chloride causes it to decompose into **..........** gas and **..........** chloride gas, and these gases recombine on cooling to reform the solid.
cards.back_md: Heating ammonium chloride causes it to decompose into **ammonia** gas and **hydrogen** chloride gas, and these gases recombine on cooling to reform the solid.

front_blocks.md: The decomposition of ammonium chloride is a reversible reaction.

back_blocks.md: Heating **ammonium chloride** produces **ammonia** and **hydrogen chloride** gases, and when these cool they recombine to form solid **ammonium chloride** again, so the reaction is reversible (NH<sub>4</sub>Cl ⇌ NH<sub>3</sub> + HCl).

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

The decomposition of ammonium chloride is a reversible reaction.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

Heating **ammonium chloride** produces **ammonia** and **hydrogen chloride** gases, and when these cool they recombine to form solid **ammonium chloride** again, so the reaction is reversible (NH<sub>4</sub>Cl ⇌ NH<sub>3</sub> + HCl).

front_blocks.md: What colour change occurs when hydrated copper(II) sulfate is heated?

back_blocks.md: **Hydrated copper(II) sulfate** is blue and turns **white** when heated as it loses its water of crystallisation to form anhydrous **copper(II) sulfate**.

cards.front_md: What colour change occurs when hydrated copper(II) sulfate is heated?

front_blocks.md: Adding water to anhydrous copper(II) sulfate is **..........**, and removing water from hydrated copper(II) sulfate by heating is **..........**.

back_blocks.md: Adding water to anhydrous copper(II) sulfate is **exothermic**, and removing water from hydrated copper(II) sulfate by heating is **endothermic**.

front_blocks.md: Hydrated copper(II) sulfate and anhydrous copper(II) sulfate are both blue.

back_blocks.md: **Hydrated copper(II) sulfate** (CuSO<sub>4</sub>·5H<sub>2</sub>O) is blue, but **anhydrous copper(II) sulfate** (CuSO<sub>4</sub>) is white.

Hydrated copper(II) sulfate and anhydrous copper(II) sulfate are both blue.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

**Hydrated copper(II) sulfate** (CuSO<sub>4</sub>·5H<sub>2</sub>O) is blue, but **anhydrous copper(II) sulfate** (CuSO<sub>4</sub>) is white.

back_blocks.md: **Water of crystallisation** is water that is chemically incorporated into the crystal structure of a hydrated salt during the crystallisation process, affecting the salt's shape and colour.

cards.back_md: **Water of crystallisation** is water that is chemically incorporated into the crystal structure of a hydrated salt during the crystallisation process, affecting the salt's shape and colour.

front_blocks.md: How can the direction of a reversible reaction be changed?

back_blocks.md: A **reversible reaction** can be made to go in the **forward** or **reverse** direction by changing the reaction **conditions**, such as temperature. Heating hydrated copper(II) sulfate drives the reaction forward (dehydration); adding water reverses it.
